content: 1. Cowpox is a viral infection caused by the cowpox virus, which is related to the vaccinia virus. 2. Vaccinia virus is a member of the poxvirus family and is used in the smallpox vaccine. 3. Molluscum contagiosum is a viral skin infection caused by a poxvirus, characterized by small, raised, and usually painless lesions. 4. Exanthema subitum, also known as sixth disease, is a viral illness caused by human herpesvirus 6 or 7, presenting with a sudden high fever followed by a rash. 5. Erythema infectiosum, or fifth disease, is caused by parvovirus B19 and is characterized by a slapped cheek rash and mild systemic symptoms. 6. Enteroviral vesicular stomatitis with exanthem is a condition caused by enteroviruses, presenting with vesicular lesions and a rash. 7. Hand, foot, and mouth disease is a contagious viral illness caused by coxsackievirus or enterovirus, characterized by sores in the mouth and a rash on the hands and feet. 8. Enteroviral vesicular pharyngitis is an infection caused by enteroviruses, leading to vesicular lesions in the pharynx. 9. Other specified viral infections characterized by skin and mucous membrane lesions include various conditions caused by specific viruses affecting these tissues. 10. Foot-and-mouth disease is a highly contagious viral disease affecting cloven-hoofed animals, not humans. 11. Unspecified viral infections characterized by skin and mucous membrane lesions refer to conditions where the causative virus is not identified. Viral Hepatitis (B15-B19): 12. Acute hepatitis A is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus, typically transmitted through contaminated food or water. 13. 14. Acute hepatitis C is caused by the hepatitis C virus, often transmitted through blood or blood products. 15. Acute hepatitis E is caused by the hepatitis E virus, primarily transmitted through contaminated water. 16. Chronic viral hepatitis refers to long-term liver inflammation caused by persistent viral infections, such as hepatitis B or C. 17. Unspecified viral hepatitis refers to liver inflammation of viral origin where the specific virus is not identified. Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Disease (B20-B24): 18. HIV disease resulting in infectious and parasitic diseases includes complications such as mycobacterial infections, cytomegaloviral disease, candidiasis, and Pneumocystis pneumonia. 19. HIV disease resulting in malignant neoplasms includes conditions like Kaposi's sarcoma, Burkitt's lymphoma, and other lymphoid or hematopoietic malignancies. 20. HIV disease resulting in other specified diseases includes complications such as encephalopathy, lymphoid interstitial pneumonitis, and wasting syndrome. 21. Acute HIV infection syndrome refers to the initial stage of HIV infection, characterized by flu-like symptoms. 22. Persistent generalized lymphadenopathy in HIV disease involves chronic swelling of lymph nodes. 23. Hematological and immunological abnormalities in HIV disease include conditions like anemia or immune dysfunction not classified elsewhere. 24. Unspecified HIV disease refers to cases where the specific complications or manifestations are not detailed. Other Viral Diseases (B25-B34): 25. Cytomegaloviral disease is caused by cytomegalovirus, leading to symptoms ranging from mild to severe, especially in immunocompromised individuals. 26. Mumps is a viral infection caused by the mumps virus, characterized by swelling of the salivary glands. 27. Infectious mononucleosis is caused by the Epstein-Barr virus, presenting with fever, sore throat, and lymphadenopathy. 28. Viral conjunctivitis is an inflammation of the conjunctiva caused by viral infections, often highly contagious. 29. Epidemic myalgia, or Bornholm disease, is caused by coxsackievirus, presenting with severe chest or abdominal pain. 30. Ross River disease is a viral illness transmitted by mosquitoes, causing fever, rash, and polyarthritis. 31. Viral carditis refers to inflammation of the heart muscle caused by viral infections. 32. Retrovirus infections not elsewhere classified include conditions caused by retroviruses other than HIV. 33. Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HPS) is a severe respiratory illness caused by hantavirus. 34. Other specified viral diseases include various viral conditions not classified elsewhere. 35. Viral infection of unspecified site refers to cases where the location of the viral infection is not identified. Mycoses (B35-B49): 36. Dermatophytosis refers to fungal infections of the skin, hair, or nails caused by dermatophytes. 37. Tinea barbae and tinea capitis are fungal infections affecting the beard and scalp, respectively, often presenting with inflammation or hair loss. 38. Tinea unguium, or onychomycosis, is a fungal infection of the nails. 39. Tinea manuum is a fungal infection of the hands. 40. Tinea pedis, or athlete's foot, is a fungal infection of the feet. 41. Tinea corporis is a fungal infection of the body, often presenting as ring-shaped lesions. 42. Tinea imbricata is a chronic fungal infection with overlapping scales. 43. Tinea cruris, or jock itch, is a fungal infection of the groin area. 44. Pityriasis versicolor is a superficial fungal infection causing discolored patches on the skin. 45. Tinea nigra is a fungal infection causing dark patches on the palms or soles. 46. White piedra and black piedra are fungal infections of the hair shaft. 47. Candidiasis refers to infections caused by Candida species, affecting various body sites such as the mouth (oral thrush), skin, nails, or genital areas. 48. Pulmonary candidiasis is a fungal infection of the lungs caused by Candida. 49. Candidal meningitis is an infection of the meninges caused by Candida. 50. Candidal endocarditis is a fungal infection of the heart valves caused by Candida. 51. Candidal septicaemia refers to bloodstream infections caused by Candida. 52. Other specified superficial mycoses include fungal infections not classified elsewhere. 53. Superficial mycosis, unspecified, refers to fungal infections of the skin or mucosa where the specific pathogen is not identified.
